chapters.title: Chapter 74: Hidden Workshop
paragraphs: Claire was stunned to see three armored vehicles...
Based on its size, she could guess that each of them could carry six or more Sentinels at the same time!
Then, she noticed that the tires were worn but intact, and the armored bodies suggested they had been built for war or survival.
There were also some dents, scratches, and faded insignias that had long since been scorched away.
Claire’s heart raced. Vehicles like these could mean mobility, supply runs, or even firepower. In this apocalypse, they were more valuable than gold.
As for fuel, they should be able to find some of them here.
She then walked closer, brushing dust from one of the doors. As she tried to open it, the hinges creaked, but the lock was still in place.
She tried looking inside with her flashlight, but she couldn’t see through it. Still, she knew that this was one of the best things they could find here!

"Should I..." Claire hesitated over whether to claim this as her own wealth or not. After all, her Fifth Sin Talent or the Spirit that came with it would be satisfied with that. However, once she claimed it, it couldn’t leave her side or her wealth inventory... or else, the benefits she would gain from it would dissipate.
Just like that, she swiftly returned to the main hall, where she saw Kai and the others dismantling the Sentinels.
"...Kai," she whispered as she approached Kai, who was busily organizing the materials taken out of the Sentinels. "You need to see this."
"Hmm?" Kai was curious, seeing how cautious she was, so he followed her.
Soon, the armored vehicles were revealed!
In the meantime, Sera and Althea moved together, and their first stop wasn’t storage rooms or other areas where wealth could be found.
The two women had a different purpose.
With their flashlights on, they passed through a corridor leading to another building. Well, they wanted to know if anyone else had been kept here or if more captives were waiting to be freed.
The memory of being chained was still fresh in their minds. They had been dragged, shackled, and forced to cover the Sentinels as living shields after all.
Being used as a meatshield to make others hesitate wasn’t something they wanted to happen again, and for others to experience it...
Just the thought of it made Althea’s stomach churn.
"This way," Sera whispered as she recalled the place through her memories.
She remembered the path vaguely.
The corridor that led to the warehouse was definitely the path they were walking on right now...
"It’s here..."
Soon, they reached the heavy doors, and Sera hesitated before pushing them open. The hinges groaned faintly, but as soon as their flashlights swept across the interior, they were stunned.
They were expecting to find several people barely hanging on or even corpses on the floor...
However, it was actually empty!
The warehouse was wide open, and its concrete floor was bare and clean!

The stench that had once suffocated them, the reek of sweat, blood, and human waste, was gone. The filth that had covered the corners, the piles of discarded rags, were gone! All of it had vanished for some reason.
However, they knew that they weren’t just hallucinating since they could still see the chains bolted into the walls... This was definitely the correct place!
Althea was confused. "This... this isn’t right."

Sera stepped forward and looked around. She remembered the exact spot where she had been chained. She remembered the cries of others, the sobs, the silence that followed when someone was dragged away by the Sentinels...
Although the place was clean, there were still the scratch marks, bolted chains, and cracked floors that made her sure that this was the right place.
This was simply too weird!
"What is going on here?" Sera muttered as she looked around.
They walked deeper into the warehouse, their lights sweeping across the walls and floor. No stains. No discarded bones... No scraps of clothing. There was truly nothing.
It seemed impossible.
"This doesn’t make sense," Althea whispered. "We were kept like livestock. Dozens of us. And now... It’s spotless."
Sera clenched her fists. "Where did they go? Where are the others?"
The silence pressed down on them...
They stopped near the center of the warehouse, where they had once huddled with other captives, waiting for the Sentinels to drag someone away.
Althea crouched, running her fingers across the floor. This was definitely the place. However, it was as if they erased everything.
"Why? Why would the A.I. army bother to clean this place? They don’t care about filth. They don’t care about us..."
Unfortunately, no one could answer them just yet.
The survivors had worked tirelessly through the night, dismantling Sentinels, sealing windows, and exploring the compound. Fatigue soon weighed on them, and Kai, decided it was time to rest.
He brought out more Shelter Gift Packs... From them, he distributed sleeping bags, ensuring everyone had a place to lie down.
The survivors settled across the halls and slept there...
Morning came quietly, and the survivors resumed their exploration. This time, they pushed deeper into the compound, searching rooms they hadn’t fully checked yet.
After all, the compound had a total of five buildings, and three of them were two-story.
Unexpectedly, in the basement of the main building, they found a reinforced door.
Victor worked the lock, and with a groan, it opened to reveal a hidden workshop, or perhaps a laboratory!
"Whoa... This looks awesome." Victor was excited. As a mechanic, he knew that all these tools and machines would help him work better.
Everyone saw rows of tools and half-finished components lining the walls. But at the center of the room stood something that made them all freeze.
They immediately pointed their flashlight on it...
It was a Mechanical Soldier!
"It’s not moving! Don’t worry!" Kai reminded everyone as they all drew their weapons.
"Whew... That scared me..."
"I thought we’re ambushed or something..."
Ralph and Wallace muttered.
Kai chuckled as he could understand why they were worried.
Unlike the Sentinels they had dismantled, this one looked so different. It looked more advanced, like those in the Sci-Fi movies!
Then, the system notification acknowledged their discovery!
[ You have discovered a dormant Sentinel (A) ]
[ Status: Unactivated ]

chapters.title: Chapter 75: The Familiar Error
paragraphs: The mechanical soldier was actually inside a capsule or chamber that was also connected to wires hanging from the ceiling and scattered across the floor.
This A-Grade Sentinel was at the center of the room, and it looked nothing like the Sentinels they had dismantled before.

It wasn’t bulky. Its frame was smooth, with barely any angular parts. It almost looked like a human wearing a full-body suit with a tight helmet. The design was advanced, far more refined than the crude shapes of the lower-grade Sentinels.
Kai stepped closer, brushing dust off the capsule. The glass was scratched, and most of the letters on it had faded. Only one word could still be read clearly: ATOM...
"Atom..." Kai muttered. "Is that the company? Or its name?"
On the other hand, Victor’s eyes widened. "This is amazing. I’ve never seen anything like it. If I dismantle it, we’ll learn so much!"
Kai raised his hand quickly. "No. Not this one. It’s different... Just focus on the low-grade ones for now."
Victor frowned but didn’t argue. He knew Kai was serious.
Anyway, the group looked around the workshop.
There were shelves filled with spare parts, like extra limbs, synthetic muscle fibers, shield, and armor for the A-Grade Sentinel! There were even crates with bladed weapons inside.
However, the most important were the rifles!
Ralph pulled one out, and he could barely carry it!
"Ahhh... This thing is heavy!"
Thud!
He immediately put it down as he realized that it was custom-made for Mechanical Soldiers and not humans.
Kai was also curious about it and inspected the item.
They just looked closer to a carbine, but it was heavier and bulkier, and it was probably meant to be carried with one hand by the Sentinels.
Still, Kai realized that the ammunition wasn’t similar to the laser or plasma that was being used by the C-Grade Sentinel before.
Wallace nodded. "I guess using those plasma rifles wasn’t that ideal, huh..."
"They probably have an issue with the production materials. The plasma rifles were definitely expensive to make," Ralph added.
"But I don’t think this weapon is worse than the plasma rifle that requires constant change of energy cells." Victor commented.
Kai just smiled at their speculations and studied the Sentinel again.
"Is this also a mass-produced Mechanical Soldier?" He muttered.
He couldn’t help but frown at that idea. After all, he could imagine that this type of Sentinel would be a terrifying opponent.
The survivors exchanged uneasy glances.
"I hope not..." Terrence replied.
The dormant machine was not moving in its position within the capsule, but they couldn’t help but see that once those wires were released, it would suddenly activate and attack them.
As a matter of fact, even without power, it was clear that the A-Grade Sentinel was something far more dangerous than anything they had faced before.
The others slowly left the workshop one by one after checking the bladed weapons and guns on the crates...
They planned to check other areas.
Soon, their footsteps faded as they returned to the main hall. Victor was the last to glance back, still itching to dismantle the Sentinel, but Kai’s warning kept him silent.
Kai and Claire stayed behind. His eyes lingered on the capsule. The system notification earlier was still bothering him.
[ You have discovered a dormant Sentinel (A) ]
[ Status: Unactivated ]

Why had the system notified them about this? It hadn’t done so when they discovered the crates of weapons, the frozen E‐Grade Sentinels in the hall, or even the armored vehicles. This was different. Too different.
"I’ll open it..." Kai muttered under his breath.
Claire, who had been waiting for him to leave the room, stiffened. She turned toward him, her flashlight steady.
"Alright... I will save you if needed," she said with confidence. She had just recently obtained wealth that boosted her Fifth‐Sin Talent, and she wasn’t afraid to use it.
Kai smiled faintly. This was exactly why he had helped Claire obtain those items. She was reliable.
He stepped forward and pressed the button on the capsule.
With a hiss, the chamber unlocked. Cold air rushed out, spilling across the floor.
The glass lifted slowly, revealing the Sentinel inside.
Kai reached out and touched the smooth surface of its armor.
Immediately, the system flared to life.
[ Contact Established: Sentinel (A) ]
[ Accessing dormant protocols... ]
[ Advanced data detected... ]
[ Synchronization in progress... ]
This wasn’t a notification coming from the Sentinel. It was from the system itself, the Apocalypse System, that brought them here!
Kai’s eyes widened as more notifications appeared one after another.
Claire tightened her grip on her weapon as she noticed Kai stepping back. "Kai... what’s happening?"
Kai didn’t answer right away. His gaze was fixed on the Sentinel, as he felt worried that it would suddenly move and attack.
After confirming that it was not, he finally replied.
"I’m getting system notifications. Are you not?"
"No..." Claire replied as she shook her head.
Kai frowned as he realized that he knew nothing about the Apocalypse System and what it truly wanted after all.
The system had never reacted like this before. This wasn’t just a discovery, it was something deeper.
The Sentinel remained unmoving, but the flood of messages made it clear: touching it had triggered something hidden.
Kai’s hand lingered on the Sentinel’s armor. The system messages kept coming.
[ Admin... ]
[ Error... ]
[ Warning: Core systems inactive ]
[ Attempting override... ]
[ Success. Awakening sequence initiated. ]
"Wait..."
Kai stepped back quickly as he saw that Admin Error again! It was the same error message that forced him to select the A.I. Rebellion!
"Is it... activating?" Claire worriedly asked.
Soon, the Sentinel’s chest emitted a faint glow as the wires around it lit up.
Then, the sound of shifting mechanisms echoed in the room.
More notifications appeared in Kai’s vision.
[ Status: Awakening ]
[ Searching for command authority... ]
[ Link established: Administrator ]
[ Recognition complete. ]
[ New Controller Registered. ]
[ Awaiting designation... Please assign a name. ]
"What... Administrator? New Controller?" Kai paused as he saw the last system message telling him to give the Sentinel a name!

I will save you if needed," she said with confidence.
She had just recently obtained wealth that boosted her Fifth‐Sin Talent, and she wasn’t afraid to use it.
Kai smiled faintly.
This was exactly why he had helped Claire obtain those items.
She was reliable.
He stepped forward and pressed the button on the capsule.
With a hiss, the chamber unlocked.
Cold air rushed out, spilling across the floor.
The glass lifted slowly, revealing the Sentinel inside.
Kai reached out and touched the smooth surface of its armor.
Immediately, the system flared to life.
[ Contact Established: Sentinel (A) ]
[ Accessing dormant protocols... ]
[ Advanced data detected... ]
[ Synchronization in progress... ]
This wasn’t a notification coming from the Sentinel.
It was from the system itself, the Apocalypse System, that brought them here!
Kai’s eyes widened as more notifications appeared one after another.
Claire tightened her grip on her weapon as she noticed Kai stepping back.
"Kai... what’s happening?"
Kai didn’t answer right away.
His gaze was fixed on the Sentinel, as he felt worried that it would suddenly move and attack.
After confirming that it was not, he finally replied.
"I’m getting system notifications.
Are you not?"
"No..." Claire replied as she shook her head.
Kai frowned as he realized that he knew nothing about the Apocalypse System and what it truly wanted after all.
The system had never reacted like this before.
This wasn’t just a discovery, it was something deeper.
The Sentinel remained unmoving, but the flood of messages made it clear: touching it had triggered something hidden.
Kai’s hand lingered on the Sentinel’s armor.
The system messages kept coming.
[ Admin... ]
[ Error... ]
[ Warning: Core systems inactive ]
[ Attempting override... ]
[ Success.
Awakening sequence initiated. ]
"Wait..."
Kai stepped back quickly as he saw that Admin Error again!
It was the same error message that forced him to select the A.I.
Rebellion!
"Is it... activating?" Claire worriedly asked.
Soon, the Sentinel’s chest emitted a faint glow as the wires around it lit up.
Then, the sound of shifting mechanisms echoed in the room.
More notifications appeared in Kai’s vision.
[ Status: Awakening ]
[ Searching for command authority... ]
[ Link established: Administrator ]
[ Recognition complete. ]
[ New Controller Registered. ]
[ Awaiting designation...
Please assign a name. ]
"What...
Administrator?
New Controller?" Kai paused as he saw the last system message telling him to give the Sentinel a name!

chapters.title: Chapter 76: Atom
paragraphs: The first Admin Error that Kai received happened during the Apocalypse Selection. The second Error happened after his Weekly Gift Cycle Talent, which was supposedly only capable of giving him three gift packs per week, was changed to Infinite Gift Pack Talent...
This time, however, the Error happened with the activation of the A-Grade Sentinel...
"What’s going on?" Claire asked worriedly.
Kai jolted and immediately explained the situation.
"I think that this thing recognized me..." He replied.
Claire’s grip on her revolver tightened. "Recognized you as what?"
Kai swallowed hard. "Its master or something... I think I need to give it a name."
As he said this, the notification lit up once more as if reminding him to focus on giving it a name.
[ Please assign a name. ]
Kai paused for a moment and looked at the capsule... Then, he made a decision.
"Atom..."
[ You have chosen "ATOM". ]
[ Confirm selection? ]
Kai then saw the Yes or No option and didn’t hesitate to select Yes.
Kai clenched his fist and nodded. "Yes."
[ Name confirmed: ATOM ]
[ Initialization sequence resuming... ]
[ Link established. ]
[ Identity registered. ]
[ Core link stabilized. ]
[ Sentinel (A) - ATOM Unit is now active. ]
[ Combat systems remain offline until further command. ]
[ Auxiliary systems online. ]
The Sentinel’s chest glowed faintly, and its helmet tilted forward as if acknowledging Kai.
Claire’s eyes widened.
"It... it moved." She said as she watched the Sentinel move out of its capsule. It stood about 2 meters tall!
Then, Kai’s vision filled with one last message.
[ ATOM has recognized Kai as its Controller. ]
[ Synchronization complete. ]
[ Future commands will be accepted only from a registered Controller. ]
Kai exhaled slowly. Without a doubt, his heart was pounding. The A‐Grade Sentinel was no longer just a dormant machine. It had accepted him!
Claire lowered her revolver slightly, though her grip remained tight.
"So... it’s yours now?" She asked cautiously. She had to make sure that this thing wouldn’t just suddenly attack them after all.
Thankfully, Kai slowly nodded. "I can control it at the very least..."
Of course, he wanted to know more about the Sentinel.
He tried speaking to it, like asking where it came from or who made its body, but there was no reply. The helmet remained silent, and no voice came out.
"It can’t talk..." Kai muttered.
Claire tilted her head. "Then how do you know it listens?"
Kai thought for a moment, then gave a simple command. "Pick up a weapon."
The Sentinel moved.
Its hand reached toward one of the crates and lifted a heavy rifle with ease. The motion was smooth, precise, and without hesitation before turning to Kai, waiting for more instructions.
Kai nodded. It was a basic instruction after all.
Claire’s grip on her revolver loosened slightly, though she still looked wary. "So it can follow orders."
Kai nodded with a hint of excitement. Now, he needed to give this thing more complicated instructions.
"Guard me as I walk around the building."
The Sentinel stepped forward, rifle in hand, and positioned itself beside him.
Then, Kai walked across the workshop and Atom followed silently... Its movements remained steady and would always be in protective position.
Kai couldn’t hide his grin. "This is incredible. It really listens."
Claire raised an eyebrow. "And what if it listens too well? What if it takes an order the wrong way?"
Kai stopped, realizing the danger. He turned back to Atom. "Then I’ll make sure it understands the rules."
He took a deep breath and spoke clearly, almost like he was teaching a child.
"Atom, listen carefully. These are the laws you must follow."

Just like that, Kai recalled the three laws of robotics... He had learned them during his elective class, Ves Robotics, back in high school. But this time, he decided to change them. The old laws wouldn’t work in this world.
"First Law... You must never harm me, Kai, or allow me to come to harm through inaction."

Claire blinked as she heard this... She really thought that Kai would give the three laws of robotics that she was aware of. However, she also realized that in this Apocalypse, other human survivors could also be their enemy.
Kai knew this very well, so he changed it.
The real first law was "You must never harm a human being, or allow a human being to come to harm through inaction."
’If humans attack us, Atom must be able to fight back. Protecting me comes first.’Kai thought.
Then, he continued. "Second Law... You must obey the commands I give you, unless those commands conflict with the First Law."
Claire wryly smiled after hearing this. At this point, she could already understand Kai’s train of thought, so she stayed quiet.
"Third Law... You must protect your own existence, as long as that does not conflict with the First or Second Law."
Kai’s voice echoed in the chamber.
Atom stood silently, rifle in hand, but then its helmet tilted forward.
A faint glow appeared where its eyes or scanners should have been.

Two sharp lines of light lit up across the visor... Then, it pulsed once before stabilizing. It didn’t end there as the glow spread faintly across its chest, as if confirming that the instructions had been absorbed.
"Whoa..." Kai was impressed by what he just saw... It was as if it truly embodied the laws he just said on a whim.
Claire also saw this and knew that this was the real deal. "It... lit up."
Kai’s heart pounded. "It worked, right?"
For some reason, he could really feel it... Atom had definitely acknowledged the laws he had given.

"Yes, definitely... It can’t speak, but it recognized the command you gave. I’m sure of it... Though your laws sound a bit too selfish, Kai." Claire said with a chuckle. She didn’t really mind the laws that Kai gave.
Kai grinned and didn’t deny it. "Well, in this world, survival comes first. If Atom can’t fight humans, then it’s useless. I need it to protect me above all else."

chapters.title: Chapter 77: Blocked
paragraphs: In Haven-45, Mila had never imagined herself leading people. She was the head of the sanitation crew, someone who spent most of her days keeping the underground base livable.

Her small team was tasked with scrubbing walls, disposing of waste, and making sure disease didn’t spread among the survivors. But after Kai and most of the fighters left to secure a new base, leadership fell to her.
Among the group left behind were two nurses, two cooks, three sanitation workers, including herself, one scout, and one boiler room operator.
None of them were soldiers. None of them had the strength to fight off another siege, but they were all equipped with a revolver.

Haven‐45 had already been battered by bombardments during the Mech Siege, and its walls were cracked and its tunnels were unstable. Every day, Mila worried that the ceiling might collapse while they slept.
Still, she kept them together.

She organized shifts, nurses helped organize the scavenged materials, cooks rationed what food Kai left for them, and the sanitation crew kept the underground air breathable. The boiler operator made sure the generators didn’t fail. Mila herself walked the halls constantly, speaking to each of them, reminding them that Kai had promised to return with good news.
After all, she noticed that some of them were already thinking that they had been abadoned after a day of not getting news!
Indeed, since the first day passed in silence and there was no word from Kai, they felt a little concerned.
Then, the second day dragged on, and fear gnawed at them. Some started arguing that maybe Kai and the others had been wiped out. Mila silenced those doubts quickly. "He will return," she said firmly.
"We just have to hold on."
Although she was also worried, she couldn’t just show it to them.
On the third day, just as despair was beginning to settle in, the sound of engines echoed faintly above ground.
At first, everyone thought it was another mech patrol and they had to stay silent and wait for them to leave.
Of course, panic spread, since Sentinels weren’t something they could defeat with mere revolvers!
However, Mila herself stood at the entrance with her sanitation crew, ready to defend with whatever tools they had if they were somehow discovered.
But then a familiar voice was heard above ground!
"Hey! It’s me! Augustine! Open the tunnel!"
As soon as they heard this, Mila’s eyes lit up, and she immediately opened the tunnel’s entrance to take a look!
Everyone was so happy after confirming that they were all doing fine!
Behind Augustine were five other Survivors who had left with them to conquer another shelter. And more than that, they weren’t alone. Two armored vehicles were waiting nearby!
The survivors froze in shock.
"So that’s the noise. But... what is this?" one of the nurses whispered.
Mila was also confused and asked a similar question. "Armored vehicles... here?"
Augustine raised his hand. "We did it. Kai is a great commander. We secured the mechanical army base. We brought these back!"

Russel, one of the scouts, couldn’t contain his pride. He patted the side of one of the vehicles and continued. "Yes... We found them in the AI army base we conquered. They’re tough and built for war. With these, we can move supplies, people, and anything we need. We’re not trapped anymore."
The group erupted in murmurs of disbelief.
The cooks stared at the vehicles as if they were treasures.
The boiler operator shook his head in awe.
Even the nurses, usually reserved, smiled at the sight of their transportation!
After all, it looked really safe to be inside one of these things!
Mila stepped forward and continued. "With these... we can finally leave, right?"
"That’s right!" Augustine said as he looked at Mila’s eyes. They had been in this shelter for many years, and although it had served its purpose well, it was already time for them to replace it.
Just like that, Mila and the rest immediately began organizing the preparations.
"We can’t leave anything important behind," she told the group.
"Yes... That’s why we brought the vehicles. Pack everything we can carry. Food, tools, medical supplies, and the plants."
The peanut plants were their lifeline if Kai could no longer magically provide resources.
It may be hardy but nutritious, and capable of growing even in poor soil. They had been carefully cultivated in Haven‐45 over the years after all.
Next came the scavenged parts, broken pieces of Sentinels and Hounds that had been collected after battles. Even damaged, they were valuable.
Victor had taught them that these parts could be dismantled for materials or even rebuilt into weapons. So Mila ordered them to be loaded into the vehicles.
The cooks then packed what remained of the rations Kai had provided before leaving. Instant noodle packs, canned goods, and sealed water containers were stacked carefully.
It didn’t end there since even the tents were rolled up, ready to be carried. Blankets, sleeping bags, and makeshift bedding were gathered.
The boiler operator also insisted on bringing spare fuel and tools. "If the generators fail in the new base, we’ll need these," he explained.
Piece by piece, the survivors carried their lives out of Haven‐45.
As the armored vehicles were loaded, the survivors couldn’t help but marvel at them.
One of the nurses touched the side of a vehicle. "I never thought I’d see something like this again. It feels... safe."
The scout Augustine grinned. "Safe and powerful. These things can carry six or more Sentinels at once. Now they’ll carry us."
Mila listened, her heart swelling with relief. For days, she had carried the burden of keeping the group alive in a collapsing base. Now, finally, there was a way out.
She then looked at the tunnel of their base...
"This is it. We’re leaving Haven‐45. We’ll join Kai and the others in the new base. We’ll survive."
Tears welled in some eyes as they heard this... Still, as soon as the journey began, they thought that they would safely arrive in their new shelter.
However, not even halfway there, they already attracted the attention of other survivors who had heard the armored vehicles passing through the uneven road.
"Russel! Someone’s blocking our path!"

chapters.title: Chapter 78: Followed
paragraphs: The armored vehicles passed the uneven road, carrying Mila and the others away from Haven‐45. Dust rose behind them, and of course, it attracted some attention.
"Russel! Someone’s blocking our path!" one of the cooks shouted from inside the vehicle.
Russel turned and confirmed their presence.
Ahead, figures emerged from the brush. At first, they looked ragged, barely armed. But then he saw the man at the front. He was a tall figure with a sword strapped to his back.
Seeing that his weapon wasn’t drawn, Russel didn’t immediately panic...
"They’re humans, calm down!" He immediately said, afraid that his team would just shoot their guns due to nervousness.
"They’re here... Humans..." Mark said as he looked at the two Armored Vehicles carrying people.

Mark had survived the fall of Haven‐39, barely escaping the Mech Siege with nineteen others. At this time, he was level 6, with his Master TalentSwordmaster. Master Rank was just below Epic, but it was above Superior.
Against humans, he was deadly.
His Swordmaster could help him cut flesh and bones. However, against Sentinels, his blade was nearly useless. He knew it even the people behind him knew it.
"You’re right, Mark... They’re people. We’re going to be safe, right?"
"Just don’t threaten them yet."
"Let Mark talk to them."
"Yes... Let me handle this..." Mark confidently said.

Apparently, when they first saw the two armored vehicles rolling down the road, they thought it was the AI army. Panic spread among them, and when they realized humans were inside, they felt that this was a bit more manageable.
Mark raised his hand, signaling his group.

Four of them were from Earth like him, dragged into this apocalypse after choosing the A.I. Rebellion scenario. The rest, sixteen noobs, were armed with crude blades, slingshots, and nets meant for Swarmers...
They were all weak, but at the very least, they were loyal to him and would always follow his command.
’It’s now or never. Either we join them... or we take those vehicles.’Mark’s jaw tightened.
Russel then slowed the lead vehicle... The others felt a bit tense, so they all gripped their revolvers just in case a fight broke out.
Mark stepped into the road, sword gleaming faintly in the sunlight.
Three others flanked him, ready to protect their leader at any moment.

Soon, Mark raised his voice. "I’m Mark! We are survivors from Haven‐39! Our shelter was destroyed. We barely escaped the last Mech Siege. We need protection. Let us join you! We have decent Talent and Skills that can help you all."
His words carried desperation. Behind him, the nineteen survivors waited nervously, clutching their crude weapons.
Inside the vehicle, Russel frowned. He wasn’t heartless, but he knew his place. He had no authority to accept refugees since only Kai could decide.
Russel shook his head. "I’m sorry. I can’t take you in. This isn’t my decision. We have orders."
Mark’s eyes narrowed. "Orders? While people die out here? You’d leave us to be slaughtered?"
Russel’s grip tightened on the wheel. "I won’t offend our Leader. I can’t make promises I can’t keep."
The others inside the vehicle stayed silent. They knew Russel was right. Kai was their commander. They couldn’t risk bringing in outsiders without his approval.
Needless to say, they didn’t take this kindly.
Mark’s face hardened.
He had also expected resistance, but hearing the refusal stung. He then glanced at his people. They were tired, hungry, desperate. If he returned empty‐handed, they would lose faith in him.
He raised his hand. Immediately, the rest of his group appeared from the sides of the road, surrounding the armored vehicles. Crude blades glinted, slingshots were drawn, nets were ready...
Mila gasped. "They’re surrounding us!"
Russel cursed under his breath. "Idiots..."
Mark’s voice rang out. "If you won’t take us in, then give us the vehicles. With them, we can survive. Without them, we’re dead anyway!"
The others shouted in agreement, they felt brave in front of their leader.
Jun, one of the survivors like Mark, stepped forward. His Talent activated and affected all his allies...
This move enchanted the crude weapons with a weak glow. Rocks hardened, blades sharpened, and the nets became more durable... This effect would only last for 10 minutes, but it was a good effect.
The sight was laughable compared to the armored vehicles, but it was enough to show they weren’t bluffing.
Russel’s patience snapped.
"You fools. Do you think you can threaten us with sticks and stones? These vehicles are worth more than your lives. Get out of the way."
Mark’s sword gleamed as he raised it. "Then fight us!"
Russel didn’t hesitate. He slammed his hand on the dashboard. "Ram them down! Don’t waste bullets!"
The armored vehicle roared forward while the second vehicle followed.
The survivors from Haven‐39 panicked. Nets flew, slingshots snapped, crude blades were thrown, but against steel plating, they were useless even after being enchanted by Jun.
The vehicles plowed through the roadblock, scattering them away!
Mark leapt aside, his sword slicing against the side of the vehicle.
Clank!
Sparks flew, but the armor held without any issues...
He cursed and rolled to his feet, or he’d get rammed by the vehicle...
The others also screamed as they were knocked aside, some tumbling into the dirt, others scrambling to avoid the wheels. Their enchanted weapons shattered uselessly!
Russel then shouted. "Out of the way! Or be crushed!"
The vehicles pushed forward and Mark’s group broke.

Mark’s teeth clenched. He wanted to fight these Survivors with his sword since he knew that it was his only advantage. Unfortunately, they weren’t ready... They didn’t have the time to create a proper block on the road and failed to stop them in the end...
Soon, the vehicles were already far away, and they could only watch helplessly.
"You’ll regret this." Mark said as he looked at the tracks left behind by the armored vehicles.
If they had a next time, they would certainly prepare something to block the road... Probably spikes, traps, anything to destroy the tires, if necessary.
After a moment of hesitation, Mark looked at his team.
They were injured, but they could recover.
After taking a deep breath, he spoke grimly... "We’ll follow them."

Dust rose behind them, and of course, it attracted some attention.
"Russel!
Someone’s blocking our path!" one of the cooks shouted from inside the vehicle.
Russel turned and confirmed their presence.
Ahead, figures emerged from the brush.
At first, they looked ragged, barely armed.
But then he saw the man at the front.
He was a tall figure with a sword strapped to his back.
Seeing that his weapon wasn’t drawn, Russel didn’t immediately panic...
"They’re humans, calm down!" He immediately said, afraid that his team would just shoot their guns due to nervousness.
"They’re here...
Humans..." Mark said as he looked at the two Armored Vehicles carrying people.
Mark had survived the fall of Haven‐39, barely escaping the Mech Siege with nineteen others.
At this time, he was level 6, with his Master TalentSwordmaster.
Master Rank was just below Epic, but it was above Superior.
Against humans, he was deadly.
His Swordmaster could help him cut flesh and bones.
However, against Sentinels, his blade was nearly useless.
He knew it even the people behind him knew it.
"You’re right, Mark...
They’re people.
We’re going to be safe, right?"
"Just don’t threaten them yet."
"Let Mark talk to them."
"Yes...
Let me handle this..." Mark confidently said.
Apparently, when they first saw the two armored vehicles rolling down the road, they thought it was the AI army.
Panic spread among them, and when they realized humans were inside, they felt that this was a bit more manageable.
Mark raised his hand, signaling his group.
Four of them were from Earth like him, dragged into this apocalypse after choosing the A.I.
Rebellion scenario.
The rest, sixteen noobs, were armed with crude blades, slingshots, and nets meant for Swarmers...
They were all weak, but at the very least, they were loyal to him and would always follow his command.
’It’s now or never.
Either we join them... or we take those vehicles.’Mark’s jaw tightened.
Russel then slowed the lead vehicle...
The others felt a bit tense, so they all gripped their revolvers just in case a fight broke out.
Mark stepped into the road, sword gleaming faintly in the sunlight.
Three others flanked him, ready to protect their leader at any moment.
Soon, Mark raised his voice.
"I’m Mark!
We are survivors from Haven‐39!
Our shelter was destroyed.
We barely escaped the last Mech Siege.
We need protection.
Let us join you!
We have decent Talent and Skills that can help you all."
His words carried desperation.
Behind him, the nineteen survivors waited nervously, clutching their crude weapons.
Inside the vehicle, Russel frowned.
He wasn’t heartless, but he knew his place.
He had no authority to accept refugees since only Kai could decide.
Russel shook his head.
"I’m sorry.
I can’t take you in.
This isn’t my decision.
We have orders."
Mark’s eyes narrowed.
"Orders?
While people die out here?
You’d leave us to be slaughtered?"
Russel’s grip tightened on the wheel.
"I won’t offend our Leader.
I can’t make promises I can’t keep."
The others inside the vehicle stayed silent.
They knew Russel was right.
Kai was their commander.
They couldn’t risk bringing in outsiders without his approval.
Needless to say, they didn’t take this kindly.
Mark’s face hardened.
He had also expected resistance, but hearing the refusal stung.
He then glanced at his people.
They were tired, hungry, desperate.
If he returned empty‐handed, they would lose faith in him.
He raised his hand.
Immediately, the rest of his group appeared from the sides of the road, surrounding the armored vehicles.

Mila gasped.
"They’re surrounding us!"
Russel cursed under his breath.
"Idiots..."
Mark’s voice rang out.

With them, we can survive.
Without them, we’re dead anyway!"

chapters.title: Chapter 79: The Lone Leader
paragraphs: Kai sat quietly in his assigned room on the second floor of the main building.
Outside, Atom stood guard, with its visor glowing faintly as it monitored the corridor.
By now, everyone in the base had learned of Atom’s presence. Shock had spread quickly, but Kai had calmed them by demonstrating how the Sentinel followed his every command without fail.
Now, alone, Kai finally decided to consume the vial of Prime Gene Enhancement Serum.
[ Prime Gene Enhancement Serum: A rare genetic resource. Permanently increases base stats upon consumption. Small chance of awakening a Gene Skill. ]
It was an item that he looted from Alex. The latter probably didn’t consume it as he reached the consumption limit and had to wait for several days. Unfortunately for him, it was now his treasure.
Thankfully, Kai had nothing to worry about. His passive gene skill, Bio Adaptive Constitution, ensured he could absorb enhancements without risk of overdose or rejection.
Kai lifted the vial, took a cautious sip, and checked the taste.
[ Prime Enhancement Serum Consumed ]
[ +1,800 Experience Points ]
[ Permanent Stat Increase: Health +90, Spirit +9 ]
It was nice...
Encouraged by the result, Kai consumed the rest of the vial in one go. Immediately, a flood of notifications filled his vision.
[ Prime Enhancement Serum Consumed ]
[ You have leveled up! ]
[ New Gene Skill Awakened! ]
[ You have leveled up! ]
[ You have leveled up! ]
[ New Gene Skill Awakened! ]
"What?! Level 15?! Wait... Did I just get two gene skills?!" Kai’s heart raced. Not only had he reached Level 15 far faster than expected, but he had also awakened two new Gene Skills...
What was even more exciting was the fact that one was passive, and one was an active skill!
Without hesitation, he quickly checked the new skills!
[ New Passive Gene Skill Activated! ]
[ Skill: Battle Trance (Level 0) ]

[ Description: When Health drops to 5% or below, the user automatically enters a combat trance. In this state, attack power and defense are greatly increased, pain response is suppressed, and survival instincts are heightened. ]
[ Note: Passive skills cannot be deactivated. Leveling requires Gene Skill Points. ]
"This is nice!" Kai muttered as he saw the Battle Trance. Though he didn’t want to be in a position where he had to resort to this method, it was still nice to know that he had a trump card.
Anyway, Kai checked the next Gene Skill...
"It’s really an active skill..."
[ Skill: Spirit Pulse (Level 0) ]
[ Description: Releases a controlled burst of Spirit Energy that can hit a target within a short radius. Consumes Spirit upon activation.
Activation Cost: 100 SP ]
[ Note: Active skills can be manually triggered. Leveling requires Gene Skill Points. ]
Kai’s eyes widened. Finally, an active skill!
It was super expensive, but it was something he could use directly in combat, not just rely on passive boosts. He clenched his fist, excitement surging through him.
He quickly opened his status screen to confirm the changes.
[ Name: Kai ]
[ Title: Survivor, Pioneer, Siege Breaker ]
[ Level: 15 ]
[ Physique Rating: D ]
[ Talent: Infinite Gift Pack (SSS) ]
[ Active Skills: Spirit Pulse Lv0 ]
[ Passive Skills: Keen Sense Lv3, Bio Adaptive Constitution Lv3, Fortune’s Favor Lv0 ]
[ Skill Points: 5 ]
Kai exhaled slowly, a grin spreading across his face. "Finally... it looks good now."
In the meantime, Arjun sat in the dim shelter of Haven‐19, he was actually very excited right now.

He had just reached Level 9, and soon he would break through to Level 10. That meant entry into the Leaderboard, the system’s public ranking that displayed the strongest survivors across the continent.
For days, only one name had been listed there... Kai.
It was depressing, almost humiliating, that no one else had managed to qualify. Arjun dreamed of seeing his own name beside Kai’s, proof that Haven‐19 had produced someone worthy.
Every night before sleeping, he checked the leaderboard for inspiration. Tonight was no different. He opened the system interface, expecting to see the same lonely entry.
But what he saw made his breath catch.
[ Leaderboard ]
1. Kai - Level 15
Arjun’s eyes widened. "H‐how?!"
He had expected Kai to still be Level 10, maybe 11 at most. But Level 15? That was absurd. Too fast! It was just too unfair.
At this point, he had no idea if someone was just messing with his mind.
Meanwhile, in Haven‐11, Mei also checked the leaderboard. She had known someone with the name Kai back on Earth, before the apocalypse selection.
When she saw his name glowing at the top, her chest tightened.
"Kai... is it really you?" she whispered.
She hoped desperately that this was the same Kai she remembered, the one who had laughed with her, the one who was always so reliable!
If it was him, then maybe there was still hope. Maybe she wasn’t alone in this nightmare.
Across the continent, reactions exploded. Survivors in scattered shelters stared at the leaderboard in disbelief.
"Level 15?! Already?!"
"This is broken! How can one person rise that fast?"
"It’s unfair... we’re struggling just to reach Level 5, and he’s already at 15!"

Some felt awe, while others felt jealousy, and many simply despaired at the sight. The gap between Kai and everyone else was starting to get too wide. Right now, he wasn’t just ahead, he was untouchable.
At this point, they could only guess what kind of situation he was in.

Some believed Kai had discovered hidden resources, perhaps a secret vault or ancient ruins filled with rare items. Others guessed he had awakened a unique Talent that allowed him to level up faster, something absurd like double experience, or even triple.
A few of them even feared that Kai had allied with the AI army itself. How else could someone rise so quickly in a world where every battle against machines was a desperate struggle?
In Haven‐7, a group of survivors really wanted to find Kai. "No one should be able to climb that fast!"
In Haven‐12, a young fighter stared at the glowing name with clenched teeth. "Kai... whoever you are, I’ll catch up. I refuse to be left behind."
Meanwhile, others simply gave up hope. "If one man is already Level 15 while we’re stuck at Level 4 or 5... what chance do we have? The leaderboard is a joke."
But no matter the speculation, one fact was undeniable...
Kai was the only name on the leaderboard. And now, he was Level 15.
Ding!
Suddenly, as everyone was thinking that they should work harder to level up faster, a system notification appeared!
[ Global Event is Back! ]

chapters.title: Chapter 80: The Currency and the Global Event
paragraphs: Kai was checking his inventory since he had also received free Survivor’s Medals after reaching Level 15...
[ Survivor’s Medal: It can be used to conduct transactions in the Gene Skill Store, with the elusive Secret Merchant, or among the Gene Traders. ]
Without a doubt, these Medals were awesome, and as a matter of fact, he was planning to use these Medals as the currency in his shelter.
Perhaps, one Survivor’s Medal would be worth 5 Gift Packs of their choice.
The only reason he was giving them for free so far was because of their situation... They also had a recent emergency since he could never survive the Mech Siege alone.
Furthermore, they were basically his employees right now.
As the leader of the shelter, he’d be able to command every member, and if they did not want his orders, they could just leave this place.
As he checked his inventory, he realized that he already had 11 of them! Most of them came from his rewards just now.
Still, the others who weren’t Survivors from Earth didn’t have any way of obtaining the Survivor’s Medal. These medals were obtained from System Rewards after all.
"Maybe Energy Cores?" Kai mused. This would certainly make them work harder... However, it might force those who weren’t even combat experts to fight the Mechanical Army and lead to their deaths.
He didn’t want them to sacrifice their lives like that.
In the end, he decided to start limiting the supplies he’d give to others, so they wouldn’t get too dependent on him...
Perhaps, he’d only provide 5 Gift Packs per day and let the managers take care of it...

’But we should really find other sources of food.’ Kai thought as they had to find some other sources of food. Since they are no longer underground, they should consider growing vegetables or even fruit trees at this point!
Then, as he was thinking of this, the Global Event Message appeared!
Ding!
[ Global Event is Here! ]
[ Upcoming Hostile Operation: Field Tyrants ]
[ Countdown: 10 days ]

[ Objective: Hunt or survive against newly deployed mechanical Field Bosses appearing across the continent. Each Field Tyrant will patrol a designated zone, forcing survivors to either avoid or confront them. ]
[ Failure Condition: Shelter population reduced below threshold due to Field Tyrant activity. ]
[ Rewards: High Experience Points, Rare Loot Drops, Survivor’s Medal, Gene Enhancement Materials, and others ]

[ Additional Notice: Field Tyrants are unique boss‐class constructs. Each of them has specialized combat procedures and devastating area attacks. Survivors are advised to form hunting parties before engaging. ]
[ Estimated Enemy Composition: Tyrant‐class Boss Units, Sentinel Escorts, Spyder Rangers ]
[ Special Reminder: Gene Traders may appear in random locations during the event. Survivors can exchange Survivor’s Medals for Gene Skills, Enhancement Serums, or rare genetic resources. ]
Every Survivors who came from Earth received the same message.
Unlike the Mech Siege, this wasn’t about defending a shelter, it was about the AI unleashing boss‐class constructs into the open fields.
These machines were designed to dominate entire regions, forcing survivors to either hide or risk everything in battle.
Shelters erupted in chaos...
"Field Tyrants?! Out in the open?!"
"We can’t just sit behind walls, can we? I think avoiding them is the best option!"
"Boss‐class units... this is suicide for low-level Survivors... Thankfully, we have ten days to prepare. At least that should be enough."

The reminder about Gene Traders added fuel to the fire. Survivors are already considering the possibility of trading their hard-earned Survivor’s Medals for Gene Skills or Enhancement Serums. For many, this was the first real chance to evolve beyond their limits. But it came with a deadly price, they would probably have to face the Tyrants first, to find these Traders.
Kai stared at the glowing notification.
"Field Tyrants... and Spyder Rangers? Is that similar to the artillery? I hope not. That’s too much. A weaker version should be enough." He mused.
Right now, his new skills, Battle Trance and Spirit Pulse, suddenly felt more vital than ever. The thought of Gene Traders appearing during the event made his heart race.
’If I can find one, I could trade my Survivor’s Medals for more enhancements. That could change everything.’
But he knew the danger.
Even without meeting them yet, boss units aren’t like Sentinels. They’re designed to crush entire groups.
"I guess Atom will be the key to this event." Kai muttered as he looked at his door, where Atom was.
At this time, Victor was in the workshop, dismantling a broken Sentinel unit, when the notification appeared. His wrench slipped from his hand when he saw it...

"Field Tyrants, Sentinels, and Spyders... What in the world are we getting into?" He wasn’t sure if this was better than Mech Siege or not. Nonetheless, he knew that if someone managed to bring down a boss-class enemy, that could only be Kai.
Victor’s eyes were filled with hope.
He could only trust the miracles that Kai could make... Perhaps, the event wasn’t just a threat, but an opportunity to make their Shelter Leader even stronger!
As a matter of fact, everyone in the New Haven-45 had similar reactions as soon as they saw the message.
Aurora was outside the shelter, carefully collecting any valuable plants, when the system message flashed before her eyes.
She froze, clutching her basket.
"Boss units... roaming the fields?" she whispered.
Her heart pounded since the open plains would no longer be safe.
Every trip outside could mean running into a Tyrant and its escorts. But then she remembered the reminder about Gene Traders.
"If I can find one... maybe I can trade for a Gene Skill. Something to help me more with the plants."
She only has two Survivor’s Medal but she was hopeful that they could be used for a trade. Then, she tightened her grip on the basket and prayed silently.
"I hope Kai will have a plan to kill that thing."
If someone could bring them to victory, that was definitely their Shelter Leader! Without a doubt, they were putting their trust in him!

’If I can find one, I could trade my Survivor’s Medals for more enhancements.
That could change everything.’
But he knew the danger.
Even without meeting them yet, boss units aren’t like Sentinels.
They’re designed to crush entire groups.
"I guess Atom will be the key to this event." Kai muttered as he looked at his door, where Atom was.
At this time, Victor was in the workshop, dismantling a broken Sentinel unit, when the notification appeared.
His wrench slipped from his hand when he saw it...
"Field Tyrants, Sentinels, and Spyders...
What in the world are we getting into?" He wasn’t sure if this was better than Mech Siege or not.
Nonetheless, he knew that if someone managed to bring down a boss-class enemy, that could only be Kai.
Victor’s eyes were filled with hope.
He could only trust the miracles that Kai could make...
Perhaps, the event wasn’t just a threat, but an opportunity to make their Shelter Leader even stronger!
As a matter of fact, everyone in the New Haven-45 had similar reactions as soon as they saw the message.
Aurora was outside the shelter, carefully collecting any valuable plants, when the system message flashed before her eyes.
She froze, clutching her basket.
"Boss units... roaming the fields?" she whispered.
Her heart pounded since the open plains would no longer be safe.
Every trip outside could mean running into a Tyrant and its escorts.
But then she remembered the reminder about Gene Traders.
"If I can find one... maybe I can trade for a Gene Skill.
Something to help me more with the plants."
She only has two Survivor’s Medal but she was hopeful that they could be used for a trade.
Then, she tightened her grip on the basket and prayed silently.
"I hope Kai will have a plan to kill that thing."
If someone could bring them to victory, that was definitely their Shelter Leader!
Without a doubt, they were putting their trust in him!

chapters.title: Chapter 81: The New Haven
paragraphs: Jonas, who came with Terrence and Aurora and was also known for his Iron Stomach Talent, was on the eastern wall, hammering planks into place with other members of the shelter, when the notification appeared.
He froze at the sight of the new event.
"Field Tyrants... roaming outside the shelters?"
"That’s dangerous."
"Thankfully, we have some time to prepare."
"But if those things targeted this place, we’ll get in trouble. I think we must prepare to escape just in case."
The others around him were also informed, and they couldn’t help but feel nervous... It wouldn’t be surprising if that kind of field boss would suddenly turn to their shelter after all.
At this point, Jonas also had no idea how their shelter leader would tackle this situation. Still, he knew that he must contribute as much as he could.

If Kai decided to raid one of these Field Tyrants, he needed to be part of it and get the experience points he needed. He didn’t need to be in a Leaderboard immediately, but he must accumulate experience points as much as he could.
"Let’s just do our part... We’ll need stronger walls. If those things come near, we can’t let them breach us so easily." Jonas said.
But deep down, he knew walls wouldn’t be enough. Boss-class machines weren’t meant to be stopped by barriers. They were meant to be hunted, or they’d get their shelter destroyed.
Across the continent, survivors debated furiously.
Some of them vowed to form hunting parties, dreaming of the rare loot and Gene Enhancements that could be theirs.

Others swore to avoid the Tyrants entirely, fearing that they had more advanced weapons that they could never deal with. After all, these Field Tyrants must definitely be equipped with stronger cannons, lasers, or something even worse that could destroy their shelter.
However, the mention of Gene Traders spread hope and desperation alike. It meant braving the fields, where the Tyrants could be waiting for them, but it should be worth the risk.
"What if by only destroying the Tyrant will those Gene Traders appear? "
"Gene Traders... Don’t expect too much. The least medals they’ll take might even be ten or so."
"What? That’s too much. I only have two medals ever since."
"Look... Someone’s already Level 15... Stop wasting time and find a way to level up."
They were all unsure how to approach this event that would come in ten days.
However, Kai already had a plan!
After some time, the residents of New Haven‐45 gathered in the central hall, forty survivors in total.
It was a bit tense due to the recent update, but they were expecting some good news from Kai.
Russel’s team had already returned with the armored vehicles and Mila’s group from the old shelter, and now Kai stood before them, ready to speak.
Of course, Russel had already reported the encounter with desperate survivors along the way and Kai agreed with his decision not to let them in.
"We can’t risk unknowns right now. This place must be secure before we expand."
Kai’s gaze swept across the crowd. He could feel their eyes on him, waiting, uncertain, but hopeful. He straightened his back and spoke with authority.

"From today onward, this place will be officially known as New Haven-45. There will be new divisions, you can no longer use the previous arrangement. To survive, we need a proper structure. I will establish divisions, each with clear responsibilities, so everyone will have a role."
Kai gestured toward Ralph.
"The Assault Division will be split into two teams. Team A will be led by Ralph. His Sharpshooter Talent makes him ideal for ranged combat."
Ralph nodded firmly.
"Team B will be led by Claire," Kai continued, turning to the woman who had proven herself in several skirmishes. "She will be supported by Terrence. Together, they will form our close‐combat unit."
The crowd murmured approval. Claire gave a confident smile, while Terrence nodded and agreed to this decision.

Kai then continued. "Your first mission is not to attack. Instead, you will organize the frozen Sentinels we’ve captured and place them outside the shelter. They may be statues now, but to outsiders they will look like mechanical soldiers standing guard. Let the world believe we are defended by machines. This can be useful for us too."
Soon, Kai’s eyes found Irene, a calm woman with steady hands.
"Irene will lead the Medic Team. She has already proven her skill in treating wounds. She will be supported by anyone with basic knowledge of first aid. If you don’t know, you will learn."
Irene bowed her head slightly...
Kai turned toward the group working in the kitchen.

"Next is the Provision Division. We need food. My Gift Packs cannot sustain us forever. From today, the Kitchen Crew will be formalized. You will manage rations, prepare meals, and begin experimenting with farming. Aurora will assist with gathering plants and seeds. We must grow vegetables, fruits, anything that can sustain us long‐term. As for the leader, Aurora should act as the leader for now."
Although their Survivor Title would allow them to survive for a long period of time even without eating, it wasn’t the case for everyone.
Then, Kai looked at Victor, who was still smudged with grease from dismantling Sentinels.

"Victor will lead the Engineering Division. His team will handle repairs, construction, and dismantling of machines for parts. This division will also oversee the armored vehicles that we have. If we can salvage Tyrant components in the future, Victor will be the one to turn them into weapons."
Victor grinned, wiping his hands on a rag. "Leave it to me."
Finally, Kai turned to Jonas, who had been hammering planks into the eastern wall, before she turned to Wallace.

"Wallace will lead the Security Division with Jonas to assist you... I also want this team to be involved with reinforcing walls, building barricades, and ensuring the shelter remains secure. But you will coordinate with the assault teams when threats approach."
"Understood!" Victor replied.
The hall was filled with agreement, but before anyone could relax, they all heard a bell ring!
Kai immediately perked up as this was the signal he taught Atom to warn them about the approach of human Survivors!

chapters.title: Chapter 82: Jammer
paragraphs: Through the tinted windows of New Haven‐45’s main building, Kai and the others immediately spotted the group approaching.
Twelve figures moved cautiously across the ruined landscape. What caught Kai’s attention at once was their appearance... they weren’t wearing Survivor Gear.
This could mean that they weren’t people brought from Earth like him and other members of the shelter. These were natives of the continent.
’So they’re not the same ones who blocked Russel’s path when he rescued Mila and the others... these are different.’Kai mused.
Of course, he also couldn’t help but feel cautious about this. After all, they had just been attacked by a mind-controller a few days ago.
However, with Atom outside, including their weapons being ready, he felt that they had an advantageous position...
This would not end well for these twelve people if they ever planned to attack them.
"Hmmm? Look at that..." Claire muttered as she looked at how confident those twelve were.
The strangers seemed aware of the shelter’s true nature. They didn’t act as if this was an AI base anymore. Instead, they waved white flags, signaling peace.
"Traders?" Wallace muttered, though his hand was already on his weapon.
Team A and Team B then moved out as get into position... Before the twelve got closer, they already had their weapons raised, ready to respond if things went wrong.

Kai studied them carefully. Ten of the figures looked like escorts... They were armed, disciplined, and clearly protecting the other two. The remaining pair carried packs that were unusually large, strapped to their backs.
"We’re not here to fight! We just want to trade!" One of the guys carrying a huge backpack shouted.

"Merchants? They’ll come just like that?" Kai was confused for a moment. Although he didn’t really want to think of these guys as NPCs, he couldn’t help but consider it for a moment. After all, who would be wandering this dangerous land to search for customers?!
Nonetheless, seeing that they weren’t here to fight, Kai signaled to the group and allowed them entry.
Soon, they entered the main hall, and Kai confirmed that the newcomers were wandering merchants... They weren’t just traders who were trying to escape from A.I. Army.
Kai calmly looked at their attire before he addressed them. "How did you find us?"

One of the traders, a lean man with blue eyes, stepped forward and gave a faint smile. "It’s not easy to find this place but before that, my name is Diego Morales, and this is my partner, Santiago Reyes. We are merchants. We travel with our escorts, ten men who keep us alive on the road."
Kai studied them closely. "I see... I’m Kai. So, can you explain how you knew we were here?"
Diego gently nodded as he expected to be questioned. It was always like this whenever they tried visiting a human shelter.
"We have detectors. They can sense human signatures. That’s how we knew there were many of you gathered in this place."
Kai frowned. "Detectors?"
He didn’t expect that there was such a convenient item to find humans! However, this was actually dangerous for them if the A.I. Army possessed this thing.

Santiago shrugged and explained. "We just inherited this thing. It was salvaged from a high-ranking mechanical soldier years ago. It’s not perfect, but it works. Anyway, we followed the trail here... though we were surprised to see Sentinels guarding the walls."
The escorts nodded as they also started glancing at the unmoving machines outside.

"Luckily," Diego added quickly, "we realized they were drained ones. Otherwise, we wouldn’t have dared to come closer. Ahem... If you want to learn more about the A.I. Rebellion that happened. You can always ask us... We can share what we know for a certain price."
Kai’s curiosity deepened.
’Scanners that can detect humans... salvaged from the AI army itself? And they even have something that can detect whether that mech soldier is active or not...’
He had many questions, but as expected, nothing would come for free.
"What do you want in exchange for answers?" Kai asked.

Diego’s smile widened. "We sell some items you might be interested in. You can buy them with Energy Cores. We need a C‐Grade or higher. Armor‐Piercing Bullets will do as well. If you have food, we can consider trading with some of our items Or..." He paused, his eyes gleaming. "...Survivor’s Medals. If you buy a lot from us, then the information is free."
Kai stiffened. "Survivor’s Medals? Are you Gene Traders?"

Santiago shook his head. "Not exactly... However, we bought some of their items and brought them here with us. We deliver goods, take risks, and earn a commission. Of course, our prices are higher because we move around constantly. But if you want easier access to Gene Enhancements, this is the way."
The hall fell silent. Survivors exchanged glances, their expressions a mix of shock and hope.
Kai’s mind raced.
’So even the natives know about Survivor’s Medals... and they were able to connect with the Gene Traders. This changes everything.’
This was too good for them... He didn’t expect that they would have traders like these.
Kai felt excited.
The Field Tyrants were coming in ten days, and now wandering merchants had appeared at his doorstep, offering rare items for them!

Kai then looked at Diego and Santiago. "Then show me what you have. We don’t have armor-piercing bullets, nor do we have C‐Grade Energy Cores. But we do have piles of food we can trade. And we also have a few Survivor’s Medals."
Diego and Santiago exchanged a quick glance, their expressions shifting from polite neutrality to genuine interest.

"Preserved food is always welcome," Diego said. "There are many shelters that would trade for it. Of course, for food, we can only offer basic goods like tools, clothing, and some medical supplies. Nothing extraordinary, but useful for keeping your people alive."
He paused, then exchanged a look with Santiago before adding, "But... if you’re willing to give us a larger share of food, we do have one special item we can part with."
Santiago carefully opened a smaller case, revealing a compact device wrapped in cloth. When he set it down, the survivors leaned closer.
"This," Santiago explained, "is a Portable Signal Jammer."

chapters.title: Chapter 83: The Other Gene Enhancement
paragraphs: "Portable Signal Jammer?" Kai repeated. He had a similar device that he got from the Enhanced Gift Pack.
However, the one that they brought here seemed to have a better effect considering its size.

"That’s right... It can disrupt AI communications within a short radius. It won’t stop any of the mech soldiers from attacking, but it can confuse drones or delay reinforcements. For shelters, it’s priceless, sometimes a few minutes of silence is the difference between survival and annihilation."
The listening Survivors were obviously impressed.
Victor, their mechanic, also gently nodded. He really wanted to take a closer look at this device...
As for Wallace and the other fighters, they were already imagining how it could be used during raids.
"That’s... actually useful." Claire muttered.
Diego smiled faintly after seeing a positive response.
"We don’t usually trade this kind of thing for food, but if you actually have enough supplies to provide with us, we’re willing to make an exception. Think of it as an investment in your survival."
Santiago didn’t push Kai and the others to immediately purchase after introducing one item. They knew that they had to continue showing what they could.
So he stepped forward, unstrapping one of the heavy packs from his back.
He laid it down carefully and opened it, revealing neatly arranged compartments.
Inside were bundles of dried herbs, rolls of cloth, sharpened knives, small vials of antiseptic, and various other tools like a hammer, hatchet, bag of nails, and others.
"These are also items we trade for food," Santiago explained.
"They’re practical items. They are things shelters often run out of, based on our experience."
Kai nodded, but his gaze lingered on the other pack... the one Diego carried.
"And for Survivor’s Medals?" Kai asked.
Diego’s smile widened. He tapped the second pack, then slowly opened it. Inside were items that immediately drew the attention of everyone in the hall...
He then swiftly explained what they were...
They were Alpha Gene Enhancement Serums sealed in glass tubes! They were the familiar gold liquid that gives a boost in status and also a small chance of Gene Skill awakening.

"These Alpha Serums were quite common, but not because they’re easy to find. It’s because they’re stable and safe for consumption. As long as you take what your body can and have the patience to wait before consuming them again, you’ll be fine..."
Kai nodded as he had already seen its effects before.
Then, Diego set down a vial filled with green liquid.

"This one is the Emerald Gene Enhancement Serum. Well, you can consider this a Bone Density Enhancement Gene... but there is a chance of mutation. Nothing extreme though... perhaps changes in skin tone, heightened senses for specific things, or unusual growths. Anyway, people who take it often gain endurance beyond normal limits... but they must accept the risk."
Kai was quite interested.
’Bone density enhancement... endurance beyond limits, but with mutation risks. That could change everything.’
With his Bio-Adaptive Constitution, he was quite hopeful that the mutation wouldn’t be too negative for him.
Anyway, the others also found this useful despite the risk of mutation.
Claire, who felt that she also needed to try getting stronger through other means, liked this.

"Stronger bones? Sounds useful... but I don’t like the idea of growing something I shouldn’t. We’re not getting tails or horns on that, right?" She joked, expecting the two merchants to smile or laugh.
However, they actually looked a bit surprised!
"Ahem... That only happens in extremely rare cases..." Diege softly replied.
Now, Claire shook her head as she realized the dangers of consuming risky Serums. The gold liquid was indeed the best out there.
Victor leaned forward and actually found the serum interesting...

"Well, if it really boosts endurance, having such side effects shouldn’t be a bad deal. It probably depends on someone... If it were me, I could dismantle machines for days without rest. That’s worth the gamble."

Since Victor wasn’t a combat type Survivor, he couldn’t be hunting Mech Soldiers for Experience Points like all the others. Instead, he could only rely on his work as a Mechanic to get the Experience Points he needed to level up.
Seeing that they understood, Santiago carefully held up a crimson vial.

"And this... is the Crimson Gene Enhancement Serum. It grants immense strength and agility, but the mutation risk is far higher. Some who take it develop aggressive tendencies, or their bodies adapt in ways that make them less human. Still, for those who survive the process, the power is unmatched."
The hall fell silent again as they considered the risk. This was definitely a great serum.
Kai then locked eyes with Diego and Santiago. "Then let’s talk prices."
Diego’s tone grew firm as he explained the costs.
"The Emerald and Crimson Serums are five Survivor’s Medals each. As for the Alpha... one vial is worth fifteen Medals."
The crowd was visibly shocked.
"Fifteen?!" Claire’s eyes widened. "That’s impossible for any of us alone."
Jonas shook his head. "Even five is too much. We’d have to pool everything we have."
Victor also felt that this was too much. "Even if we do so, only two or three of us would get a chance."
Kai raised his hand, silencing them. He understood the temptation, but the price was simply too steep. "We won’t rush into this. Not now..."
Diego and Santiago nodded knowingly. They had seen this hesitation before.
Kai then shifted the discussion. "Let’s focus on what we can trade with food. We have canned tuna and instant noodles. How many of these for the Portable Signal Jammer?"
As he said this, Kai showed the canned goods and instant noodle packs.
Diego’s eyes gleamed. "One hundred canned goods. One hundred packs of noodles."
The survivors gasped at the cost.
Kai’s expression hardened. "Impossible. We don’t have that much, and even if we did, I wouldn’t give it all away. You’ll have to lower your demand."
Diego crossed his arms as if he were trying to see how much food they could bleed out.
"Well... This device is rare. We risked our lives carrying it here. It’s worth the price... I promise you. I’ll even add a map for you!"

sentences.text: "Portable Signal Jammer?" Kai repeated.

However, the one that they brought here seemed to have a better effect considering its size.
"That’s right...
It can disrupt AI communications within a short radius.
It won’t stop any of the mech soldiers from attacking, but it can confuse drones or delay reinforcements.
For shelters, it’s priceless, sometimes a few minutes of silence is the difference between survival and annihilation."
The listening Survivors were obviously impressed.
Victor, their mechanic, also gently nodded.
He really wanted to take a closer look at this device...
As for Wallace and the other fighters, they were already imagining how it could be used during raids.
"That’s... actually useful." Claire muttered.
Diego smiled faintly after seeing a positive response.
"We don’t usually trade this kind of thing for food, but if you actually have enough supplies to provide with us, we’re willing to make an exception.
Think of it as an investment in your survival."
Santiago didn’t push Kai and the others to immediately purchase after introducing one item.
They knew that they had to continue showing what they could.
So he stepped forward, unstrapping one of the heavy packs from his back.
He laid it down carefully and opened it, revealing neatly arranged compartments.
Inside were bundles of dried herbs, rolls of cloth, sharpened knives, small vials of antiseptic, and various other tools like a hammer, hatchet, bag of nails, and others.
"These are also items we trade for food," Santiago explained.
"They’re practical items.
They are things shelters often run out of, based on our experience."
Kai nodded, but his gaze lingered on the other pack... the one Diego carried.

Diego’s smile widened.
He tapped the second pack, then slowly opened it.
Inside were items that immediately drew the attention of everyone in the hall...
He then swiftly explained what they were...
They were Alpha Gene Enhancement Serums sealed in glass tubes!
They were the familiar gold liquid that gives a boost in status and also a small chance of Gene Skill awakening.

It’s because they’re stable and safe for consumption.

Kai nodded as he had already seen its effects before.

"This one is the Emerald Gene Enhancement Serum.
Well, you can consider this a Bone Density Enhancement Gene... but there is a chance of mutation.

Anyway, people who take it often gain endurance beyond normal limits... but they must accept the risk."
Kai was quite interested.
’Bone density enhancement... endurance beyond limits, but with mutation risks.
That could change everything.’
With his Bio-Adaptive Constitution, he was quite hopeful that the mutation wouldn’t be too negative for him.
Anyway, the others also found this useful despite the risk of mutation.
Claire, who felt that she also needed to try getting stronger through other means, liked this.
"Stronger bones?
Sounds useful... but I don’t like the idea of growing something I shouldn’t.
We’re not getting tails or horns on that, right?" She joked, expecting the two merchants to smile or laugh.
However, they actually looked a bit surprised!
"Ahem...
That only happens in extremely rare cases..." Diege softly replied.
Now, Claire shook her head as she realized the dangers of consuming risky Serums.
The gold liquid was indeed the best out there.
Victor leaned forward and actually found the serum interesting...
"Well, if it really boosts endurance, having such side effects shouldn’t be a bad deal.
It probably depends on someone...
If it were me, I could dismantle machines for days without rest.
That’s worth the gamble."

Jonas shook his head.
"Even five is too much.
We’d have to pool everything we have."

"Even if we do so, only two or three of us would get a chance."
Kai raised his hand, silencing them.

"We won’t rush into this.
Not now..."
