Thanks to that, she was able to go according to her plan...
The A.I. army soon grewfrustrated, if that was the right term, as they started smashing through obstacles while chasing her traces!
Finally, the Field Tyrant stepped onto the weakened ground, and it was followed by the Sentinels!
Crack!
The trap worked!
The earth had soon collapsed beneath the Tyrant’s weight, sending it crashing into the canyon.
Mei had already prepared explosives scavenged from the laboratory.
She triggered them, and the blast tore into the Tyrant’s exposed furnace!
Boom!
Soon, she saw the machine trying to get out or move away, but its vents started spewing fire!
Then, there was a second explosion that came from the Field Tyrant itself!
This time, it was actually a lot stronger to the point that Mei believed that she would not be able to loot anything at all!
Then, soon, the system messages flooded her vision.
[ Enemy Unit Destroyed: Field Tyrant (C) ]
[ +8,000 Experience Points ]
[ Enemy Unit Destroyed: Sentinel (D) ]
[ +1,000 Experience Points ]
[ Enemy Unit Destroyed: Sentinel (D) ]
[ +1,000 Experience Points ]
Then, she had indeed leveled up!
[ You have leveled up! ]
[ Level: 10 ]
[ Health Points +100 ]
[ Spirit Points +2 ]
[ Physique Rating has improved! ]
[ Inventory Slots Expanded: +1 ]
"Finally!" Mei clenched her fist in excitement as she read through the messages.
[ Congratulations!
You have entered the Leaderboard! ]
[ Current Rank: #3 ]
[ Congratulations!
You are the third survivor to reach Level 10. ]
[ Reminder: Rankings will be recalculated every 30 days. ]
[ Maintain your position for 30 consecutive days to receive an Exclusive Reward. ]
Mei felt extremely excited...
She had done it.
Against all odds, she had defeated a Field Tyrant alone!
Although she used a trick, it was something that others could never copy because of the terrain and timing.
She had achieved something incredible!
The victory was more than just numbers.
It was proof that she could fight, that she could carve her place in this brutal world.
’Living Camauflage...
I knew it.
This isn’t just for escaping.’ Mei thought as she soon, she felt something off.
She had a Gene Skill called Full Sense...
It allowed her camouflage talent to become more difficult to detect, but it also enhanced her senses...
’Shit...
The Spyders are still active!’ Mei recalled and looked around.
Then suddenly, she saw a flash of light!
Her Full Sense was triggered, so she swiftly moved away!
Boom!
Her previous position was obliterated by a beam of light.
The ground where she had stood moments earlier was scorched black!
"Alright... time to move," Mei whispered as she calculated the angle of attack...
Soon, she sprinted toward cover, moving through the terrain to break the Spyders’ line of sight.
Using her camouflage, she blended into the rocks and trees, vanishing from any of their angle of attack.
Thankfully, she had already leveled up, and she had full Spirit Points once again.
"Please don’t just shoot blindly..."
For now, she could only pray that they wouldn’t do something stupid like firing in her specific direction to force her out.
That would be a disaster!
Then, after several minutes of silence, Mei could finally smile a little.
She had still succeeded in her mission!
Although the Spyders were still around the area, she was already satisfied with the fact that she had reached Level 10!
As soon as Kai and the others finished salvaging the wreckage, they wasted no time retreating back to their stronghold, New Haven‐45.
The haul was heavy, but they were all satisfied with their work.
Everyone was eager to return, hoping for rest and perhaps even a surprise encounter with the elusive Gene Trader.
Kai himself had some anticipation.
The system had hinted that the Gene Traders could appear randomly, and he prayed this would be their lucky day.
But when the gates of New Haven‐45 came into view, his hope quickly soured.
The perimeter alarms were already activated, the basic wires they set up had already been cut off, and some simple traps had also been triggered.
Then, they heard the survivors on watch were shouting in panic!
Various figures moved, attempting to scale the walls...
However, what was surprising was the fact that they were not Sentinels, not Spyders, but something far more unsettling.
Kai frowned at the sight...
Although they were lucky that the siege had just started and they arrived in time, he was also confused by what he was seeing!
These weren’t machines.
They were human... or at least they had been.
They still looked human at first glance with two arms, two legs, and a head... but something was clearly wrong.
Their bodies had changed in unnatural ways.
Their limbs were uneven, their features distorted, their movements stiff and strange!
It was like they were seeing undead creatures instead!

chapters.title: Chapter 96: The New Enemies
paragraphs: Mila had always taken pride in her work, even if others overlooked it.

As head of the Sanitation Crew, she and her team were responsible for keeping New Haven‐45 livable. Toilets, floors, the junkyard, even the foul corners of the shelter... nothing was beyond their reach.

In this A.I. apocalypse, infection or sickness could be just as deadly as a Sentinel’s plasma blast. Medicines were scarce, and even when found, they didn’t always work. Cleanliness was survival, and Mila knew it better than anyone.
When her daily duties were finished, she never wasted time.
She trained with the weapons, determined not to be helpless if danger came.

During the ten-day wait for the Global Event to hunt Field Tyrants, she practiced with a revolver. At first, her shots were clumsy, but after twenty or thirty minutes of steady drills each day, her aim began to improve.
She wasn’t a soldier yet, but she was no longer just a cleaner at this point...
If Kai called for her to stand in the ramparts, then she’d be willing to do so...
After training, she often turned to the workshop.
It must be remembered that Kai had purchased rolls of fabric from wandering merchants, and those had already been sewn into comfortable clothes for many survivors.

But the ten Leather Bundles Kai had obtained from his Material Treasure Chest were different. They were thick, stubborn, and difficult to handle. Mila was the only one with the patience and skill to work them.
She spent hours cutting, stitching, and shaping the leather, turning it into protective gear and sturdy accessories.
Although her hands were calloused, she was unshaken and continued working with them/. Every piece she crafted was something she was truly proud of...
Then, just as she was finishing another piece, the alarm blared.
Mila froze while she still had the needle in her hand. The shrill sound echoed through the shelter, followed by some frantic shouts.
She swiftly followed the others outside and saw the movements of the enemies!
"Huh?" Mila was confused, seeing that the enemies weren’t the A.I. army.
"What in the world am I seeing? Are we being attacked by demons?!" She asked in surprise.
A few minutes later, Kai’s team had similar reactions!
"What am I seeing here?" Terrence was shocked as he spotted dozens of ugly-looking humanoid figures clawing their way up the shelter’s walls.
"Maybe a mutation due to radiation or something?" Claire muttered, as she couldn’t find any explanation.
Perhaps, if these figures were half-robots, she could understand that they were being controlled by the Anima Civilization or the A.I. Rebel Aria.
However, that was definitely not the case, considering how they look.
"Nah... probably result of consuming expired Gene Enhancement Serums," Ralph replied while already raising his revolver.
"We should help them... by putting them down."
None of them were panicking since they could see that the Security Division led by Wallace was actually doing perfectly fine...
They had enough ammunition, and the enemies weren’t scaling fast enough either.
They saw that everyone, including the ones in the Engineer Division and the Sanitation Crew were actually fighting really well!
Of course, it was also thanks to the wall and the barbed wire they had arranged before.
Kai clapped his hands to get everyone’s attention.
"Alright. It’s not the Gene Trader. Just shoot them. They’re not wearing armor. Do not engage in close combat. They can be dangerous."
Soon, the mutated humans shrieked as they scrambled upward...
"Open fire!" Kai commanded.
The Assault Teams unleashed a hail of bullets.
Ralph’s revolver thundered with each shot...
Needless to say, his aim was precise thanks to his Talent...
Soon, he dropped one abnormal humanoid figure after another.
Everyone swiftly followed, and it didn’t take long before themutantsscreamed as their bodies collapsed against the walls, but they seemed truly desperate!
They were ignoring pain, clawing forward even as their limbs were torn apart.
It was getting dangerous!
"Keep the pressure up!" Kai shouted...

This time, he fired his own weapon as well. As for Atom, Kai decided not to command it yet since there could be others lurking around. They must have someone who could watch their backs or flanks, and Atom was perfect for the task...
Soon, Kai and the other Survivors got the message they needed to see.
[ +400 Experience Points. ]
[ +450 Experience Points. ]
[ +380 Experience Points. ]
They were actually getting experience points from killing these abominations!
Since they were surprisingly easy to kill, everyone could only wish that more of them would spawn!
Just like that, the battle raged for several minutes... Thankfully, Kai had been very diligent and opened plenty of Weapons Gift Packs, allowing them easily overpower the enemies!
The ugly mutants had numbers but no tactics. They threw themselves at the walls like mindless animals, only to be shot down again and again.
One particularly large mutant, its body swollen with bulging muscles, managed to leap onto the barricade.
It roared, swinging its massive arms wildly in hopes of killing the guards, but Wallace was able to deal with it after throwing hatchets at its chest and head!
Thud! Thud!
Kai saw this, and he couldn’t help but feel impressed... Wallace was so calm handling that situation!
Then, it was at this point that he heard Claire and Ralph, shouting in joy behind him!
"Wooohooo! Level 10, baby!" Ralph cheered in joy.
"I got there first! I just planned to surprise you later!" Claire said.
The other Survivors saw this as well, but unfortunately for them, they hadn’t obtained any C-Grade Energy Core or something similar just yet.
Because of that, they couldn’t break through, no matter how many Experience Points they had, since their physique couldn’t handle it.
Kai could only congratulate them briefly before turning his attention back to the enemies...
Finally, after what felt like an eternity, the last mutant fell.
Thud!
Its body tumbled from the wall, joining the pile of corpses littering the ground.
Then, as Kai thought that they could finally rest, they felt the ground tremble!
Kai had a bad feeling about this as he turned around...
What he saw made him stop in his tracks. A huge Mech Unit was moving slowly toward them, its heavy steps shaking the ground.
It was another Field Tyrant, and it seemed larger this time... Furthermore, it was heading straight for New Haven‐45.
"Shit..." Kai was worried.
If the machine continued on its path, their new shelter would be destroyed. The defenses they had built would never hold against something of that size and power...
They had to stop it before it could reach their shelter!

chapters.title: Chapter 98: Hale
paragraphs: Their eyes widened in shock.
Through the haze of smoke, they saw a figure of a man...
He was wearing what seemed like a slim full-body armor. Furthermore, it seemed like he had covered most of the people on the wall, shielding them from the worst of the missile barrage.
Apparently, two of the projectiles that would have been fatal had been intercepted by him, his armor was scorched but intact!
"Ahhh... That person."
"Isn’t that the guy we saw before?!"
Indeed, this was no ordinary survivor. The figure was an Augmented Human. He was fully equipped with advanced armor and weapons.
After hearing the others’ commend, Kai also recalled the man.
This was one of the warriors who had eliminated an Ascendant Unit of the Anima Civilization not too far from their shelter!
Kai couldn’t recognize the man’s face, but as the smoke cleared, the uniform was unmistakable.
Soon, the Augmented Human removed his helmet, revealing a Caucasian man with black hair, a thick moustache, and a beard.
His features showed how tough he was, as if he was weathered by battle. Nonetheless, he still looked to be in his mid-thirties.

"I only managed to cover this small area..." the man said, gesturing to the six survivors he had protected from the blast. Among them were Wallace and several others who had been directly in the missile’s path.
As for the rest of the Security Division, they were buried in the rubble.
Kai’s mind raced with questions.
Who was this man? Why had he appeared here, at this exact moment, to save them? Was he part of another shelter nearby and was instructed to save them, or acting alone?
But before he could speak, a sharp sound cut through the smoke.
A whistle.
Kai’s eyes widened. He recognized it immediately.
Every survivor had been given a whistle from his Survivor Gift Pack, a simple tool to signal distress or location.
The sound meant that people were still alive beneath the rubble.
"Rescue them!" Kai shouted immediately.
He turned away from the Augmented Human for now. The man didn’t seem to be a threat, and saving his people came first.
The survivors rushed forward, pulling away debris, lifting shattered beams, and digging through the dust.
Wallace, still shaken but alive, also joined the effort. His Iron Stamina Talent and current level had certainly helped with his quick recovery.
Everyone else also worked together to clear the rubble, including Mila and her sanitation crew...
Minutes passed in desperate labor.
Finally, three survivors were pulled free, coughing and bruised but alive. Relief swept through the group, as the others couldn’t help but cheer with this successful rescue.
But the joy was tempered by tragedy. Three others had not survived. Their bodies were found crushed beneath the collapsed barricade, beyond saving.
Kai stood silently as the survivors gathered around the fallen.
His chest tightened at the sight of the lifeless bodies...
Every loss weighed heavily on him, since they didn’t have a large number to begin with.
He also recognized these hardworking men...
He clenched his fists, forcing himself to remain composed.
"We’ll honor them," he said quietly. "But right now, we need to rebuild."
The Augmented Human watched from a short distance with an expression that was unreadable.
He had saved six lives, but Kai could sense there was more to his presence than chance.
Finally, Kai approached him. "You saved Wallace and the others. For that, I thank you. But I need to know... who are you and why are you here?"
The man’s dark eyes met Kai’s.
He seemed to be considering whether to answer truthfully or not.
Then, after a few moments, he replied.

"I’m Hale. As for my affiliation, I can’t tell you that. But I was tracking the Tyrant. It had already been damaged in battle before it reached your shelter, right? Since you found it and seemed capable of eliminating it, I gave it up... but when it launched those missiles, I had no choice but to intervene."
Kai studied him carefully. It certainly matched what he had noticed. The Tyrant had indeed shown signs of prior combat. But this situation was just too suspicious.
"Is your shelter nearby? I think we saw your battle a few days ago."
"Shelter? Hmm... At that time, you can say so." Hale replied.
This only confused Kai, but he had a lot more things he had to do.
"We’ll talk later," Kai said firmly. "Right now, my people need me."
The man nodded, stepping back. "Do what you must. I’ll remain here for a while."
"You’re not going to take our loot, right? That Field Tyrant and its parts are ours." Kai reminded.
Hale finally chuckled after hearing this.
"Alright. I won’t covet what your little group has."

Kai smirked before he turned to his survivors. The wall was damaged, but not beyond repair. The wounded were being treated, the dead were being mourned, and there were already some people trying to rebuild their wall.
The battle against the Field Tyrants was just starting, but they already had three casualties. That didn’t seem like a good sign at all.
Later that night, after the chaos had settled and the wounded were being treated, Kai retreated to his workshop.
Atom followed him inside, its sensors active, standing guard to ensure the Augmented Human wouldn’t try anything reckless.
Hale entered quietly while looking around the workshop...
Of course, Kai kept his eyes on him, wary.
He had thanked Hale earlier, but trust was not something given so easily.
Hale, however, seemed unconcerned by Atom’s watchful stance.
He studied Kai for a long moment before speaking.
"Have you been chosen?" His tone was serious, almost solemn.
Kai frowned. "Chosen?"
He was confused.
"Yes," Hale said, his gaze shifting briefly to Atom before returning to Kai.
"Can you tell me the titles you hold right now?"
Kai hesitated.
His titles wereSurvivor, Pioneer, andSiege Breaker.But what was Hale talking about?
What did "chosen" mean?
It struck Kai then... this man hadn’t appeared by chance!

chapters.title: Chapter 99: The System
paragraphs: Kai didn’t want to reveal too much information about himself.
Even though Hale had saved Wallace and the others, he wasn’t comfortable giving such detail so easily.
Titles were part of his identity, part of the strange system that only he and a handful of other "Foreign Survivors" seemed to possess. Sharing them with someone he barely knew felt reckless.
Kai’s eyes narrowed. "Why do you want to know my titles?"
Hale chuckled after seeing how cautious Kai was.
"If I wanted to hurt you, it would’ve happened already... You’ve seen what I can do. I’m stronger than your entire group combined."
Atom seemed to have noticed that Kai suddenly tensed, so it shifted slightly with its sensors locking onto Hale. However, the Augmented Human didn’t flinch. He seemed almost amused by the suspicion.
He then raised his hand...

"I’m not here to take your loot or your shelter," Hale continued. "I’m searching for someone... someone with a title connected to being chosen by the A.I. Civilization, or perhaps by some A.I. superpower. That’s all."
Kai frowned, his confusion just deepened.
"Chosen? Titles? How do you even know about them?"
He then realized something really important... "Right... Since you know about the Titles, do you have one as well? Do you have a system like ours?"
Kai remembered what Russell, Augustine, and the other members of Haven‐45 had told him. They didn’t have access to the Global Apocalypse System.
They couldn’t see their stats, their titles, or their progression the way he could. That was what made Foreign Survivors different. So how could Hale know about Titles?
Hale’s expression softened. He smiled knowingly, as if he had expected the question.
"That’s true," he admitted. "We don’t have access to the mysterious system said to be a blessing from the Lord of the Realm. We learned that only Foreign Survivors like you could use it."
’Lord of the Realms? Isn’t that from the message we received at the beginning of the Apocalypse?’Kai thought as he recalled the familiar name.
Furthermore, Kai also realized that Hale seemed to be aware that they weren’t from this world at all.
At this time, Hale paused before reaching into his pocket.
"So... with this crystal, we can see our own status." He revealed.
Kai’s eyes widened. "You can see your stats with that?"
"Yes," Hale said simply.
He held up a faintly glowing crystal with its surface etched with strange markings.
"It’s not the same as your system, but it allows us to measure ourselves. To know where we stand."
Kai leaned closer. He was curious about this item...
He had never seen anything like it.
Hale raised the crystal, and a translucent screen shimmered into existence before them.
"Here," he said. "I’ll show you mine, as a sign of goodwill."
The display revealed Hale’s information in a format eerily similar to Kai’s system interface:
[ Name: Hale Libra ]
[ Title: Veteran, Conqueror, Defender, Warlord, Aria’s Enemy. ]
[ Level: 80 ]
[ Physique Rating: A- ]
[ Active Skills: Gene Burst Lv4, Cellular Regeneration Lv3, Neuroshock Strike Lv5 ]
[ Passive Skills: Enhanced Musculature Lv6, Accelerated Healing Lv5, Combat Instinct Lv7 ]
Kai was shocked to see this...
Although it was missing the Talent part of the stat, it was still incredible!
For a moment, he couldn’t speak. He was trying to process what he was seeing.
Kai’s curiosity sharpened the moment he saw Hale’s final title...Aria’s Enemy.
Aria was a familiar name.

She was the A.I. Rebel of human civilization, a rogue intelligence supposedly instigated by the Anima Civilization, the A.I. empire from beyond this world. If Hale had earned that title, it meant he had truly eliminated a significant number of Aria’s soldiers.
Kai chuckled as he confirmed that Hale was indeed a friend. He couldn’t help but ask, "So... you probably caused a lot of trouble for Aria... Did you destroy their base or something?"
Hale laughed after hearing this.

"Yes... If you destroy a few of Aria’s bases, you’d probably earn that title too. It’s not as glamorous as it sounds... It’s a long campaign or endless battles against machines that don’t tire. They never stop coming."
Kai studied him carefully.
The man wasn’t boasting, he was speaking from experience.
Still, Hale didn’t forget why he was here. His gaze returned to Kai.
"Now... tell me your titles."

Kai smiled since Hale’s sincerity was undeniable. He had saved Wallace and the others, revealed his own stats, and spoken openly about Aria. Kai no longer had a reason to avoid the question, so he decided to reveal them. "Survivor, Pioneer, Siege Breaker."
It wasn’t impressive compared to Hale’s list.
Hale didn’t speak immediately and studied Kai’s face... After a few moments, he nodded.
"So you’re really not him..."
Kai tilted his head. "Not who?"
Hale exhaled...
"I thought you might be the one I was searching for. You’re controlling Atom, an A‐Grade Sentinel. That alone made me suspect you were the chosen individual. But your titles don’t match."
Kai nodded. Now, he couldn’t help but feel curious about the person he was searching for.
Seeing that Hale was already planning to leave, Kai acted immediately as he wasn’t about to let Hale simply walk away. "Wait. Before you leave... that crystal. I need it. Can I buy it from you?"
Hale raised an eyebrow. "The crystal?"
Kai nodded. With that item, anyone could see their own status, even those without the system. It was something that could change everything for his people.
It would be a great help!
But as expected, Hale shook his head.
"It’s expensive. It’s not something I can just hand over. If you want one, you’ll need to find the Gene Trader. He’s the only one who deals in these crystals."
Kai’s eyes lit up.
He didn’t expect this mysterious existence to be mentioned, yet the more he thought about it, the more it made sense.
"The Gene Trader... do you have any idea where to find him?

chapters.title: Chapter 100: The Tyrant
paragraphs: Kai was already aware from the system’s notification that the Gene Trader would appear at random locations.
Still, it didn’t hurt to ask... perhaps the Augmented Human in front of him knew something the system hadn’t revealed.
Hale’s reply came after a short pause.

"If you’re serious about finding him, check the areas where Field Tyrants have spawned. Traders often linger near places where dangerous variants appear... it draws attention, and it is where customers come looking for resources."
Kai nodded after hearing this.
However, Hale wasn’t finished yet.

"If not there, search the ruins. Shady places, broken structures, anywhere the sunlight doesn’t reach. The heat drives them underground. They prefer to wait in the shadows for those who know how to look."
Kai nodded, committing the advice to memory. The Gene Trader sounded elusive, but at least now he had a direction.
Finally, Hale adjusted his armor, preparing to leave.
But before stepping away, he gave one last warning.

"Be careful. The Tyrant you fought was only one type. They’re all called Tyrants, but each variant is different. The one you eliminated carried missile launchers. Others rely on flamethrowers, some wield specialized claws that can tear through thick steel, and there are other versions like one with heavy armor, that make them nearly indestructible. Each one is deadly in its own way."
Kai nodded grimly as he already guessed that much after experiencing the missile launchers a while ago.
The thought of facing more Tyrants, each with unique weapons and abilities, was daunting. But it was better to know than to be caught unprepared.
"Thank you," Kai said sincerely.
Hale gave a small nod...
He wasn’t sure how long Kai’s small shelter could survive, but he wanted to give him a chance to survive longer.
Then, without another word, he turned and disappeared into the night, leaving Kai and Atom alone in the workshop.
Kai exhaled after the high-level human had finally left...
The Gene Trader. The status crystal. The warning about Tyrants.
Hale’s visit had been brief, but he had learned a lot of things... Still, he now had more questions than answers.

Nonetheless, Kai knew one thing for certain, Hale’s arrival was no coincidence. He had a feeling that there was more to it. He just couldn’t prove it yet, just like how he had gotten so many Errors from the system before.

Meanwhile, as most of the residents of the shelter were already resting, Victor sat hunched over his workbench, the dim light of the shelter’s workshop glinting off the twelve Energy Cores that were laid out before him.

Eight of them pulsed faintly with a deep crimson hue... They were the Tyrant Energy Cores, salvaged from the wreckage of the missile-bearing machine they had destroyed and the one with the cannon and claw...
The other four glowed with a softer blue. They were Sentinel Energy Cores... They were far more common and less volatile.
Of course, they weren’t obtained from the D-Grade Sentinels since only C-Grade could have such cores.
Instead, these four came together with the Field Tyrant, who had launched missiles.
"It must be spare energy cores for its Plasma Cannon or something." Victor guessed.
For now, however, he was in a dilemma...
He rubbed his hands together, and soon, grease and soot stained his palms.
"The Tyrant cores... too rare to waste. They’re worth more than we can imagine. Better to save them for something greater."
Victor carefully separated the cores, sliding the Tyrant ones into a special case. Their energy signatures were unstable, and he knew they could power far more than simple weapons.
Because of that, they would remain untouched for sometime.
Instead, he turned his attention to the Sentinel Energy Cores.
He then turned his attention to the four Sentinel Energy Cores.
Soon, he fitted one into the charging port of a Plasma Rifle.
The weapon gave a low hum as the core’s energy began to flow through its circuits.
"Nice..."
Victor adjusted the stabilizers, checked the gauges, and slowly directed the power until the rifle’s indicator light turned green.
Sweat gathered on his brow as he worked, but his movements were careful.
After all, this was a dangerous task.
Every connection was tested, every reading verified. He knew a single mistake could overload the rifle, but his hands were steady.
One by one, the weapons lit up, their charge indicators glowing in sequence.
"Good," Victor muttered, satisfaction in his voice. "At least these will be ready when the next fight comes."
Elsewhere in the shelter, Claire sat alone, her eyes half‐closed as she whispered to the unseen presence only she could hear.
"Are you still there?"
The spirit’s voice was faint, but she could hear it clearly reply.
They weren’t discussing anything important, just fragments of random conversation.
The spirit teased her about the way Victor looked at her when she wasn’t paying attention...

At other times, the spirit asked her what she thought of the food rations, mocking the bland taste and joking that even the machines outside probably had better fuel. Claire laughed softly, though she knew no one else would understand.
Still, she really couldn’t help but feel amaze with the spirit that she was talking with.
Her Talent, Fifth Sin, weighed heavily on her mind even after all this time. She believed it meantGreed, though she still didn’t understand its full implications.
’Was the spirit tied to that sin? Would I be devoured if I kept using the skill?’
These were some of the questions in her mind.
The next morning, Kai stood at the edge of the shelter, surveying the walls and the traps that were still unfinished.
The Field Tyrant Hunt was still not over since it was a ten-day event!
Anyway, Kai couldn’t afford to send everyone out of the shelter to hunt the Field Tyrants or search for the Gene Trader.
Defenses had to be repaired, and the shelter needed to remain secure.
Soon, Kai decided to send only the scouts to look at the areas where they might find the Gene Trader!
